title: Stream the export
summary: The CSV export works for every account except the biggest: 400,000 orders takes the container to its memory limit and the process restarts mid-download. Send the same bytes to a client that reads slowly, without the memory going with them.

checkpoints.title: The export downloads as a CSV file
checkpoints.hint: Nothing on the response says what it is, so a browser guesses and renders it. Set Content-Type and Content-Disposition before the first byte goes out: after that the headers are gone and setHeader throws.

checkpoints.title: Every row arrives intact
checkpoints.hint: A customer called Halden, Ross & Co is two columns wide. Wrap any field holding a comma or a quote in double quotes and double the quotes inside it. If the file arrives short instead, the loop stopped rather than waited.

checkpoints.title: Nothing piles up behind a slow client
checkpoints.hint: write() came back false and the loop kept writing. It does not mean the write failed: the row was taken and queued, and the response is telling you its buffer is full, so every row written past that one is memory. Wait for a drain after a false write, and only after a false one. Yielding with setImmediate is not a substitute, because giving the loop a turn does not make the client read any faster.
